Not Recommended (From Someone Who Actually Played the Game)

I’ll just get this out of the way first so it’s clear this isn’t a “skill issue” review: I was S rank in every role. I’ve put in the time. I’ve seen the systems. I understand how this game works — which is exactly why I’m done with it.

Let’s start at launch, where things immediately went great. By “great,” I mean persistent connection issues that lasted from release all the way through halfway into Season 1 (yes, the second ranked season). This wasn’t some mysterious edge-case bug — it was basic poor optimization and bad servers. A fantastic first impression for a competitive live-service game.

Then there’s the monetization, which deserves a slow clap for sheer audacity. The game technically rewards premium currency… at a blistering pace of 10 gems per week, while a single new character costs 250 gems. Since launch — including events — I’ve earned 165 gems total. Incredible. At this rate, I might unlock a character sometime next decade.

The star collection progression system somehow makes things even worse. Long-term players are actively punished for playing early. With recent changes, anyone who played since launch essentially overpaid for every hero they unlocked, by at least 250 gems’ worth. And that’s being generous, since this only accounts for the level 31 change that now allows unlocking Season 1 characters.

Oh, and let’s not forget: it was originally intended that you would never be able to unlock newly released characters through star collection — only the previous season’s. This was only changed after backlash, not because it was a bad idea (it was), but because players noticed. Always a good sign.

Hero leveling costs scale exponentially, while zeni — the standard non-premium currency — trickles in at a comically low rate. Translation: the longer you play, the harder progression becomes. For context, leveling from 1–109 costs the same as 109–119. That’s not balance — that’s a punishment loop.

Balance-wise, new characters arrive feeling hilariously overtuned. SSJ4 Vegeta in particular feels like a panicked overcorrection to SSJ3 Goku, and it paints a very clear picture of how future releases will be handled. And wow, what a coincidence — Season 1 characters got nerfed right as Season 2 launched. Totally unrelated, I’m sure.

What’s truly impressive is how every single season introduces new, innovative ways to make the game worse for F2P players and active players. Which is fascinating, because those are usually the people you want to keep in a live-service game. Bold strategy.

As for gameplay: don’t expect creativity. This isn’t even as fun as Pokémon Unite. Scoring and backcapping barely matter. Towers barely matter as long as one is still standing. Deaths and XP feel irrelevant most of the time. The optimal strategy is to play defensively, avoid risks, and wait for objectives — because doing anything else is just asking to lose. It feels less like a MOBA and more like a diet League of Legends with fewer options and less agency.

And before the Dragon Ball fans show up to explain that “they need to make money”: spare me. Literally every other successful F2P game figured this out years ago. Monetization does not have to come at the expense of fairness, progression, and player goodwill.

The devs here didn’t just miss the memo — they ignored it entirely.

Don’t play this. It’s greedy, restrictive, and steadily getting worse the more you engage with it. And that’s coming from someone who really, genuinely tried.

Now they default to giving you 1000 zeni every day you log in. Which is enough to star unlock a new character twice if you get enough of their shards (shards are given for playing that character.) This is to incentivize you to play new characters instead of just sticking to one or 2.

Which leads to EVERYONE trying to play those roles and queue times go crazy as nobody wants to queue as any role except that specific role so they can unlock a free character. (This needs to change. Make it "play with the 'any' selection 10 times. Much healthier.)

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

If you ever played a MOBA, like Leauge of Legends or Dota 2, you will find things easy to adapt. There are no items, instead you get cards that you can choose from. Not a lot of selections, so its pretty easy to choose, and you can choose anywhere on the battlefield when you unlock one.

Levels matter a LOT in this game. if you are 1 level below your enemy, prepare to know what it feels like to get the Yamcha treatment. If you are equal in level, it can come down to skill. If you are a level over them, you can greed for a kill. Tactics DOSE play a heavy role in this game, such as positioning and blind firing attacks into areas you THINK they might be to do surprise damage before they even know you exist.

All in all, fun game 8/10. Fix that character unlocking system and It'll be 9/10. What's holding it back is that there is only a single map right now, and there is no incentive to play the other game modes as they give no rewards (last time I played them anyways.)

Gekishin squadra is a fantastic MOBA. 

The average playerbase is...less than fantastic, however. 

Much like any team oriented game, Toxicity is rampant, and the amount of overblown drama-farming is outright inane when it comes to character balance or the (Honestly, very tasteful) microtransactions present in the game (It is a free to play game after all.)

I've played for 50 hours, and I've put a whole $20 into the game. I own every character, and pretty much every color for every character, along with many other cosmetics such as unique finisher moves, MVP screens, emotes, ect. And that $20 was more of an impatience thing than a "Getting something that you can't get for free" thing.

I can admit, I am blessed to play with some of the funniest, coolest players, an entire full-stack team of amazing players who have hundreds more hours than I do, and play nightly, some even top 1000 worldwide players. (Keep in mind, this game doesn't exist only on steam.) 

This makes the play experience SO much cleaner, but I have spent time solo queue and I can absolutely admit that it's the same kind of hellish pain as playing league of legends, except no amount of ranking can save you from Elo hell. It's all Elo hell, because ranking is fairly easy with a decent team with competent players.

I will use this moment to plug that I am actually writing a guide which will be showing up shortly in the Steam guides tab soon for the game with help from those same players, along with my decades (Yes, Decades. I'm old. I know.) of experience in MOBA's in general.

The main things I LOVE about this game:

• It's completely free to play, and P2W is nonexistent. No character ever launched has ever been so problematic that a little thinking, a little consideration, and a little learning of the matchups has been impossible to beat. Nothing is single-handedly winning people games. You can max out your entire account in no time, and many of the "meta" characters are part of your starting lineup. Also, the developers of the game CONSTANTLY pour free rewards down our throats. If you simply LOG IN AND DON'T EVEN PLAY you can get half of the characters in the game in like a week, and you get to choose what characters you get, and the more characters you have, the faster you level up.

• The core gameplay of the game is simple to pick up, difficult to master. Generic statement I know, but it's true. The game simplifies a LOT of the mechanics from other MOBA games to the point. No mana mechanics mean abilities are flowing constantly. The depth comes from knowing how to synergize your abilities with your allies which adds a lot of options for teambuilding. No two teammates have an identical gameplan.

• The characters are STUFFED with references. When you play Trunks, it feels like you're playing Trunks. When you play Buu, you feel like you're playing Buu. The moves, the voice lines, the synergies, the emotes and win-screens all OOZE with ...well...character! ANY character you can play, you can take one look at their ability list and your response will be "Yeah, that sounds about right".

• The developers continue to constantly tweak, fix, and adjust the game to keep it fresh and interesting. Bosses change, events bring easy ways to earn rewards, and any rough patches since season 1 have been completely smoothed out, such as Getting enough Zenny to level, making it so that when you unlock all characters of a tier, you get a character of the next highest tier, and so on.

• The way you unlock characters and the way progression works means the longer the game goes on, you get easier access to more characters. Characters go from "gems only" for a short time into Tier 1, then Tier 2, and Tier 3 and so on,  Not only that, you get Gems for free weekly, so you can farm battle passes, you can farm gem costumes, I've even gone so far as to buy multiple battle passes for free, as well as a couple of characters all from just free gems and rotating battle pass rewards.

The ONLY negative I can say about this game is the playerbase and the sloptubers who will call everything ever "Broken" before they even touch the game, and it results in an endless parade of clowns who will dive a tower and feed the enemy team because someone is playing a character they don't own, because in the minds of these people, if you own a character they don't own yet? It's OP. It's carrying you.

If they finally get it? It's clearly nerfed into the ground because it isn't carrying them for free. That mentality is such a toxic waste dump and it's caused a lot of unwarranted negative reviews. People will post factually incorrect things such as "I can't unlock X character because there's not enough character unlock nodes on the progression tree" or "Gems improve your matchmaking odds" or nonsense like that. Please. Use your brains. Use common sense.  REALLY look at the mechanics of the game. 

Because you know what? Despite everyone's complaints about new characters, when you ask the best players, the players who actually go out and win hundreds of games a week? They'll tell you the same things:

Play with friends, Play who you like. Play using common sense. Play to your teams synergies. Be aware of the opponents synergies. And Surrendering is only reasonable when you have entirely AFK teammates who have full-send given up and are crashing out.

I understand they want us to feel more immersed in the gameplay, but you can't just turn this game into a game like Xenoverse and expect people to accept it and love it without knowing that it will cost you the vast majority of the player base. The people who have stuck around and played Squadra since the beginning (like myself) play it for the bird's eye MOBA format the game is in, not the third person MOBA you are forcing us to comply with. It is one thing to rework a character, but it is completely different when you rework the ENTIRE GAMEPLAY EXPERIENCE!


 I hope that the Gekishin Squadra developers see this and greatly take this into consideration. Players don't stay no matter what happens to a game. If a change occurs and the people don't like it then the game dies. So if the season 8 overhaul comes out then I hope the players do the right thing and let this game die.

I was looking forward to the release of this game. Even though it wasn't playable for a while, I didn't overhype it or set my expectations too low; I was just waiting. I played it on both mobile and PC (using a different account), and my impressions are highly negative.
1) Terrible Optimization
The optimization is awful. My phone gets incredibly hot only when playing this game; in any other game, it barely gets warm. Here, I literally have to use a phone cooler to keep the temperatures down. On PC, it gets moderately hot, which is still somewhat tolerable.
2) Awful Matchmaking
The matchmaking takes forever and is poorly balanced. Even if you are Rank A, the game might pair you with Rank D players or literal beginners who have no idea what they are doing, leading to an instant loss. To make matters worse, you can get a bot on your team that constantly throws by running into enemy towers and dying, feeding the opponents and making them stronger.
3) Broken Balance
Balance is the most crucial aspect of any MOBA, but here, every new character is completely overpowered compared to the rest. They dominate the meta for at least a month before getting nerfed.
Furthermore, if you lose just one early-game fight, you are highly likely to lose the entire match. The enemy instantly gets a level advantage and stronger abilities, allowing them to freeze your lane and steal your farm. You can’t do anything about it, especially with a bot teammate constantly feeding.
As for bosses and cards: once the enemy secures a boss, it gives them a massive advantage that is impossible to counter if you behind from the early game. Regarding the cards, honestly, only the damage-oriented ones are actually useful; the rest feel completely pointless.
4) Role Imbalance
If you are playing solo, you are practically forced to play as an Attacker. Other roles are completely useless on their own. In a genre where teamwork is supposed to be key, this game simply rewards whoever deals the most damage.
That’s all from me.

Until proper matchmaking is implemented, solo queue toxicity is addressed, and the monetization model is rebalanced, I can’t recommend this game in good faith.

For everyone wondering why your teammates are so dumb or why every match is just a one sided blow-out for one team, it's because the game purposefully matches you with bots. Sometimes you get the bots on your team and sometimes you get bots on the other team.

The game clearly has EOMM (Engagement Optimized Matchmaking) and these bots are their poor way of implementing it.

The bots have existed since the playtests and continue to plague nearly every single match. We know that there were bots in the playtests not just by the obvious bot way they were playing, but because they all had names of the NPC characters from the 3DS game Dragon Ball Fusions, made by the same developers of Gekishin Squadra. As far as I'm aware they've stopped doing this naming convention in the official release to try and make it less obvious that you're playing with bots.

I am S rank (the highest rank you can achieve in the game) in the Technical role and the bot problem never went away, even at the highest rank in the game.

Here are just some of the ways you can tell you are playing in a bot match:

- Teammates cycle through characters extremely fast in the selection screen, and all of them get ready shortly after you do
- They never pick a preferred lane
- They pick the most random helpers. If you see both your dps pick metallic despite no buns, or your tank pick Icarus, get suspicious
- Whenever Zeno is arriving at the enemy tower, one of the bots will consistently ping that tower, exactly once
- Bots have bizarre pathing towards the lane at the beginning of the game
- If you are going top, the bot will go too far up and then have to go back down again at the first minion, instead of going to it in a straight line
- If you are going bottom, if you kill the minions before the cell jrs spawn, the bot will suddenly attempt to go top, presumably because there are no objectives to go to in bot lane, then suddenly turn around when the cell jrs spawn
